newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Indian Ocean states to launch regional trade group.
newsitem.headline: Indian Ocean states to launch regional trade group.

text.p: Fourteen Indian Ocean states meet in Mauritius from Wednesday to launch the Indian Ocean Rim Association for Regional Cooperation (IORARC) to boost trade between them.

The IORARC took shape in Mauritius last September when the 14 states agreed on a charter for the new grouping to increase cooperation in investment, infrastructure, tourism, science and technology and human resource development as well as trade.
It started as the Indian Ocean Rim Initiative of government, academic and business leaders from Australia, India, Kenya, Mauritius, Oman, Singapore and South Africa.
At its last meeting in September, the regional association's membership was enlarged to include Indonesia, Madagascar, Malaysia, Mozambique, Sri Lanka, Tanzania and Yemen for a total of 14.
Ministers will meet until Friday on this archipelago of four small islands to put life into the project.

"The principal goal is to get to know each other and to lay down the base of the organisation. Up to now it has been a forum but now it's an organisation," Mauritian Foreign Minister Paul Berenger said.
He said the meeting would decide on the IORARC's secretariat, its first heads of state summit, the possibility of expanding its membership and an application from France.
"All countries agree on the need of a secretariat and most of them agree for it to be based in Mauritius. But some think we should work a little first, before setting up the secretariat," he added.

Berenger said in September Oman proposed to host the first heads of state summit. "If Oman officially makes the proposition now, Mauritius will back it. If not, Mauritius will make its own proposition," he said.

France has applied for membership through the island of Reunion, which is an overseas department of France with the status of a region. The IOR's charter says membership is only open to sovereign Indian Ocean states.
"The charter of IOR says that new members will be chosen with consensus. Mauritius will discuss the application of France with the other members during the meeting," Berenger said.

In March 1995, the initial seven member states agreed in principle that the 30 countries bordering on the Indian Ocean were eligible to join the association but that its membership would be stabilised for a few years after it reached 14.
"This meeting will confirm whether this (stabilisation) will be done," said Berenger, adding Seychelles, Thailand, Pakistan, and Iran have already also expressed interest in the IORARC.

An Indian Foreign Ministry document said on Tuesday: "The Indian Ocean rim constitutes between a quarter and a third of world's population -- close to two billion -- carries half of world's container ships, one-third of bulk cargo traffic and two-thirds of world's oil shipments," the document said.
